To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nuclear equation of State (EOS) is important for astrophysics and that it can be constrained by selected observables in nuclear reactions.

(1) the nuclear equation of State (EOS) is an essential ingredient in the description of nuclear matter properties; (2) the nuclear EOS has an important impact on the dynamics of heavy-ion collisions; (3) the nuclear EOS is a key ingredient for understanding the structure of compact objects, such as neutron stars, and the astrophysical phenomena related to them; (4) the nuclear EOS plays an important role in the understanding of the dynamics of supernova explosions and their nucleosynthesis
the nuclear equation of State (EOS) can be constrained by the observables of the heavy ion collisions at the intermediate energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the properties of nuclear matter and its equation of state (EoS), which is the relation between energy and density, at high baryon chemical potential, and with the transport of energy and momentum in heavy ion collisions at relativistic and ultra-relativistic energies.

the EOS for asymmetric nuclear matter is still not fully understood, and more experimental and theoretical efforts are needed.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclear EOS has a soft symmetry energy at normal nuclear matter density.
the EOS for nuclear matter is soft and stiffening with increasing density.
the EOS of symmetric nuclear matter is soft, while the EOS of neutron matter is stiff.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EOS is not well determined by the observables that we studied, even if one assumes a specific model for the EOS.
the nuclear EOS can be constrained from medium energy heavy ion collision data.
the nuclear EOS is not a simple function of density and isospin.
